description: Nous somme ravis de pouvoir participer.
summary: FirePulse is an open web platform and harmonization pipeline that turns 25 years of raw NASA satellite thermal detections (MODIS C6.1 and VIIRS Suomi-NPP/NOAA-20, 2000–2025) across Gabon and its 9 provinces into consistent, interpretable series and a 2026–2035 forest-fire outlook. Raw satellite comparisons mislead for two reasons: switching from 1 km MODIS to 375 m VIIRS in 2012 creates an artificial ×3.9 jump in counts, and 38.4% of recorded detections inside Gabon come from type 2/3 sources or type-0 detections inside 183 persistent 0.05° candidate cells (mostly coastal/offshore). FirePulse isolates those candidate persistent sources, aligns pre-2012 MODIS to the VIIRS S-NPP scale using a power-law log1p model blind-tested on 2020–2025 (-74% MAE, raw R² = 0.918), prepares the post-November 2026 NOAA-20 relay, and adds an interactive 3D globe, calendar, territory map, and calibrated 2026–2035 climatological outlook with explicit scientific limits.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?

FirePulse addresses the multi-sensor continuity break between NASA FIRMS MODIS Collection 6.1 (~1 km, 2000–2025) and VIIRS Suomi-NPP / NOAA-20 (375 m, 2012–2025 archive) over Gabon and its 9 provinces (285,013 detections inside Gabon borders; 292,589 total ingested records). Raw counts distort reality in two ways: (1) switching from MODIS to VIIRS in 2012 triggers an apparent ×3.9 jump in detections due to sensor resolution, and (2) 38.4% (109,513 detections) are excluded by the full persistent-source filter: 20.3% (57,934) NASA type 2/3 detections and 18.1% (51,579) type-0 detections located inside 183 candidate 0.05° persistent cells.

FirePulse isolates these candidate cells, trains a power-law log1p calibration across the 2012–2019 overlap to map MODIS onto the VIIRS S-NPP scale, and evaluates performance out-of-sample over 72 months (2020–2025), cutting MAE from 460.3 to 120.8 detections/month (-74%, raw seasonal R² = 0.918, anomaly R² = 0.788, q80 empirical coverage 63.9%; live DB series follows the v2.0 all-years mask protocol with MAE 100.9). Users explore the results through a scroll-driven 3D globe (Three.js), switchable MODIS/S-NPP/NOAA-20 charts, a 25-year seasonal calendar (with provincial synchronization), a MapLibre GL 9-province map, automatic EN/FR detection, and an MVP 2026–2035 forest-fire climatological outlook per 0.25° forest cell (Beta(1,4) climatology on 2012–2025 VIIRS + conservative provincial trend; 2020–2025 holdout ROC-AUC 0.898, PR-AUC 0.755, Brier 0.098).

What benefits and intended impact does it have?

Without sensor harmonization and persistent-source filtering, forest managers, conservation teams, and researchers risk mistaking a satellite camera upgrade or coastal/offshore heat sources for wildfire surges. FirePulse provides documented seasonal baselines (main dry season July–August, short dry season February–March, anomaly tracking) alongside explicit methodological caveats, and prepares the post-November 2026 Suomi-NPP → NOAA-20 continuity bridge (2018–2019 calibration ratio 0.940; 2026 real-data validation pending), scalable to the Congo Basin.

What tools, programming languages, or software did you use?

- Frontend: Vue 3, TypeScript, Vite, Three.js, MapLibre GL, GSAP ScrollTrigger, Vitest.

- Backend & Geo-Database: Python 3.12, Django, Django REST Framework, PostgreSQL 16 + PostGIS 3.4, Docker Compose, Gunicorn, verified offline JSON fallback snapshots.

- Data Science & Pipeline: Python ETL/validation scripts, GDAL, NumPy, SciPy, Pandas, ESA WorldCover forest mask processing.

How is your project creative, and what factors did the team consider?

Instead of burying harmonization math in static tables, FirePulse turns multi-sensor physics into immediate visual storytelling—from a 3D globe down to Gabon's 9 provinces, with light-to-dark heat intensity and an outlook explorer. We specifically accounted for look-ahead bias (testing a frozen pre-2020 mask), cloud-cover and non-causal detection caveats (type 0 is a product classification, not ground-verified ignition cause), bilingual EN/FR accessibility, and offline resilience.

Use of Super Intelligence (SI) Disclosure:

Super Intelligence / AI models (Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Gemini 4 Argon, Deepseek 4.1 Flash 1017, Claude Opus 5.5, GPT 6 Luna, and GPT 6 Terra) were used to assist software engineering, harmonization pipeline structuring, UI/UX implementation, and EN/FR documentation. All 292,589 hotspot detections come strictly from authentic public NASA FIRMS MODIS C6.1 and VIIRS archives; zero synthetic detections or NASA branded logos/insignias were used.
